VCU psychology students, under the guidance of Dr. Marcia Winter, conduct research demonstrations on the museum floor, sharing insights from studies done through the National Living Lab network. Later in the semester, students will also conduct a live research study on children’s pre-writing skills with families who provide consent, coordinated by Dr. Virginia Chu from VCU’s Department of Occupational Therapy.

column1: Visitors are welcome to stop by to observe the demonstrations and learn about the research process and, if interested, participate in a one-on-one live study.

Please note: This is not a general museum activity. Participation in the live study is one-on-one and limited to one family at a time. Visitors are welcome to stop by to observe the demonstrations and learn about the research process.

Richmond Ballet presents Peter and the Wolf

column1: featuring the Richmond Ballet Studio Company and Trainees

Introduce the next generation to the joy of ballet with Peter and the Wolf, a beloved classic reimagined and expanded by Richmond Ballet Artistic Director Ma Cong. Follow Peter and his animal friends on a thrilling adventure to outsmart a mischievous wolf and discover that courage and teamwork can overcome even the greatest challenges. Unique to this production is a prologue filled with even more fairytale characters, including the Three Little Pigs and Little Red Riding Hood.

This family ballet, created for children and designed to appeal to audiences of all ages, is an engaging 45-minute performance that combines expressive choreography, narration, and moments of audience interaction. Featuring all-new costumes and sets by internationally acclaimed and award-winning designers, Peter and the Wolf offers a magical first ballet experience and a memorable adventure for the whole family.
Tickets are $25 (including online convenience fee). Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.
Peter and the Wolf is funded by the generosity of an anonymous donor

Live comedy. True Stories. Completely unscripted.

Richmond Famous is the city’s premier storytelling and improv show, featuring an all-star cast of Coalition performers and your favorite Richmond celebrities. Each month we welcome a new Richmond-area citizen as our featured guest. The guests share true stories from their lives, which the cast use as inspiration to create a hilarious comedy show right before your eyes!

Joining us this month is Leslie Lilburn of Leslie and the Dots! Leslie is a Northside singer-songwriter who grew up in scenic Front Royal, VA and moved to Richmond in 2021. Leslie's musical fingerprint bears traces of a unique combination of inspirations, including the British Invasion and Country music of the 60's/70's. The result is an assortment of songs infused with joy, beauty, and heartbreak that would be at home in a Tarantino film score. He passes his time in a well-appointed garage studio, Murphy’s Pocket, with his band, The Dots.

Leslie and The Dots released their debut, self-titled album on March 19, 2026. You can catch them playing all around the Richmond area. Among other events, Leslie and The Dots have been featured in the Shockoe Sessions Live and Bellwether Garage concert series.
Cast: Josh Blubaugh, Jess Brooks, Chandler Brooks, Hannah Clark, Laurel George, Purnam Jantrania, Matt Micou, David Pijor, Katie Samuelsen, Kathryn Schmidt

A completely improvised musical where every lyric, every note, and every dramatic plot twist is made up on the spot - just for you.

From The Top is a completely improvised musical where every lyric, every note, and every dramatic plot twist is made up on the spot—just for you. Now with a regular monthly slot - every second Friday of the month at 9pm!

Armed with nothing but a single audience suggestion and sheer confidence, our cast will create a brand-new musical from scratch. Will it be a sweeping romance? A high-stakes adventure? A deeply emotional ballad about a sentient loaf of bread? Only one way to find out.

The Saturday Matinee is a monthly improv comedy show featuring your favorite local performers and comedy at a reasonable hour. Come catch a show before dinner and be home in your favorite PJs by bedtime!

Each Matinee features long form improv comedy from two ensembles: one preexisting Richmond improv team and one Team from a Hat, made up of a selection of improvisers chosen at random at the previous month’s show.

What is long form improv, you ask? Good question! It is theater that is entirely made up on the spot. To your eyes, it will feel like a short play or sketch show. You may even wonder, at times, if the performers are using ideas they came up with beforehand and practiced together. But trust us, none of it is pre-planned. Come witness the magic.
October Team from a Hat Cast: Fig, Stephen Haselhorst, Wyatt Johnson, Adam Royster, Madeline Smith, Rogue Syrena, Shelby Ware, Alexandra Williams
October Team from a Hat Coach: Nate Shepherd
Team from a Hat – Rules for Entry

· Are you an improviser who would like to be on next month’s Team from a Hat? Signing up is easy! All you have to do is come to the Saturday Matinee and throw your name in the Hat. At the end of the show, we will draw eight names to join forces and become next month’s Team from a Hat.

· To sign up for a Team from a Hat, you must have completed the basic improv curriculum at any comedy theater. For example, if you trained at Coalition, you must have completed the classes through level 401. No other experience is required.
· Each Team from a Hat is provided a dedicated coach for the month and will have three rehearsals together leading up to that month’s show. Rehearsals will be on Mondays at 7:00 to 9:00 p.m.
· Members of the current month’s Team from a Hat must wait one month (i.e., to the next show) to put their name back in the Hat.
· NOVEMBER INFO: The next show will be November 14. The coach will be Josh Wright. Team from a Hat rehearsals will be October 26, November 2, and November 9.
Questions about the show? Email nate@nateshepherd.com.

column1: Classes at CMoR will be “drop-in style!” What does that mean? Simply join us on the 2nd Tuesday of the month @ 3:30PM.

Baby Artsplay!™ is a FREE program through Greater Richmond Wolf Trap offering children ages 3-36 months, along with their parents and caregivers, the opportunity to learn strategies for incorporating singing, dancing, drama, and other multi-sensory activities into their daily routine to increase engagement and support learning.
Baby Artsplay!™ is a program of Richmond Performing Arts Alliance. To learn more, click here: https://rpaalliance.com/baby-artsplay/

No pre-registration necessary. Space is limited and admission to the class is limited to 15 children and their caregivers.

Three great acts in one great show!
It's an improv triple threat trifecta triumvirate!
3x the comedy! 3x the laughs! 3x the fun! Bring 3 of your friends for this three-ring-circus of improvisational talent!

Act I: Hot Computer, established circa summer 2023, is an independent team of Coalition improvisers. You might recognize them from your favorite house teams or sketch teams. Their fast-paced improv is sure to delight all five of your senses!

Act II: Power Nap - Drift away to the dulcet tones of Power Nap, an improv troupe that’s perfect to study/relax to! Moving Art Two: Elevation
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
Moving Art Two: Elevation welcomes audiences into a world of contemporary ballet designed to stir the senses and elevate the unexpected.
Music by Lhasa de Sela

Ode is a breathtaking exploration of kinetic energy, space, and human connection by Katarzyna Kozielska. A prominent voice in contemporary European ballet, Kozielska has created works for leading companies including Tulsa Ballet, Czech National Ballet, and Chemnitz Ballet. Shaped by her long career with Stuttgart Ballet both on and off the stage, Kozielska’s distinctive choreography unfolds through expansive movement and expressive lyricism.

Artistic Director Ma Cong brings Melodia, an evocative work inspired by the music of acclaimed singer Lhasa de Sela, to Richmond Ballet. This 2007 creation harnesses the passion of the human voice to capture the profound beauty of shared experiences.

Classical technique meets a vibrant, modern landscape of shifting geometry in COLORFORMS by celebrated San Francisco Ballet soloist Myles Thatcher. This sought-after creator, whose work has been commissioned by renowned companies including New York City Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Scottish Ballet, transforms movement into a living work of art in this visually striking ballet.

CHAMPIONS open mic is the 4th Thursday of every month, hosted by Sarah Ahmed, Esther Bilderback, Grayson Bullock, Nadine Donnachie, and Taylor O'Sullivan. And oh, this night is full of surprises.
CHAMPIONS will be crowned at the end of every night. What for? You may ask. YOU WILL SEE.

Moving Art Two: Elevation
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
Moving Art Two: Elevation welcomes audiences into a world of contemporary ballet designed to stir the senses and elevate the unexpected.
Music by Lhasa de Sela

Ode is a breathtaking exploration of kinetic energy, space, and human connection by Katarzyna Kozielska. A prominent voice in contemporary European ballet, Kozielska has created works for leading companies including Tulsa Ballet, Czech National Ballet, and Chemnitz Ballet. Shaped by her long career with Stuttgart Ballet both on and off the stage, Kozielska’s distinctive choreography unfolds through expansive movement and expressive lyricism.

Artistic Director Ma Cong brings Melodia, an evocative work inspired by the music of acclaimed singer Lhasa de Sela, to Richmond Ballet. This 2007 creation harnesses the passion of the human voice to capture the profound beauty of shared experiences.

Classical technique meets a vibrant, modern landscape of shifting geometry in COLORFORMS by celebrated San Francisco Ballet soloist Myles Thatcher. This sought-after creator, whose work has been commissioned by renowned companies including New York City Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Scottish Ballet, transforms movement into a living work of art in this visually striking ballet.
Tickets start at $31*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

Moving Art Two: Elevation
at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
Moving Art Two: Elevation welcomes audiences into a world of contemporary ballet designed to stir the senses and elevate the unexpected.
Music by Lhasa de Sela

Ode is a breathtaking exploration of kinetic energy, space, and human connection by Katarzyna Kozielska. A prominent voice in contemporary European ballet, Kozielska has created works for leading companies including Tulsa Ballet, Czech National Ballet, and Chemnitz Ballet. Shaped by her long career with Stuttgart Ballet both on and off the stage, Kozielska’s distinctive choreography unfolds through expansive movement and expressive lyricism.

Artistic Director Ma Cong brings Melodia, an evocative work inspired by the music of acclaimed singer Lhasa de Sela, to Richmond Ballet. This 2007 creation harnesses the passion of the human voice to capture the profound beauty of shared experiences.

Classical technique meets a vibrant, modern landscape of shifting geometry in COLORFORMS by celebrated San Francisco Ballet soloist Myles Thatcher. This sought-after creator, whose work has been commissioned by renowned companies including New York City Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Scottish Ballet, transforms movement into a living work of art in this visually striking ballet.
Tickets start at $31*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.

column1: Stories in Motion is a program that mixes literary and dance-based movement to help children learn to connect with stories by moving their bodies! This class is designed to be unique to CMoR and was created with all kids in mind! We can’t wait to move with you!

The Nutcracker
with Richmond Symphony at Dominion Energy Center
Choreography and Original Direction by Stoner Winslett
Step into a world of enchantment where holiday dreams come to life.

Richmond Ballet’s beloved production of The Nutcracker returns to delight audiences of all ages with stunning choreography, lavish sets and costumes, and Tchaikovsky’s iconic score played live by the Richmond Symphony. Join Clara on her magical journey to the Kingdom of Sweets in this cherished annual tradition.
Saturday, December 5 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 6 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Saturday, December 12 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 13 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Saturday, December 19 – 2:00 PM and 7:00 PM
Sunday, December 20 – 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM
Tickets start at $33.60*. Visit etix.com or call the Richmond Ballet Box Office at 804.344.0906 x224 open M-F from 11:00am-6:00pm.
*this price includes facility and online convenience fees
The runtime for this performance is approximately 2 hours including one 20 minute intermission.
Please note: Strobe lighting and smoke effects are used in the production.

Richmond Ballet does not offer separate pricing for children. Each guest age 2 and up must have a ticket. Ticket prices are subject to change based on availability.

Baby Artsplay!™ is back at CMoR!

column1: Classes at CMoR will be “drop-in style!” What does that mean? Simply join us on the 2nd Tuesday of the month @ 3:30PM.

Baby Artsplay!™ is a FREE program through Greater Richmond Wolf Trap offering children ages 3-36 months, along with their parents and caregivers, the opportunity to learn strategies for incorporating singing, dancing, drama, and other multi-sensory activities into their daily routine to increase engagement and support learning.
Baby Artsplay!™ is a program of Richmond Performing Arts Alliance. To learn more, click here: https://rpaalliance.com/baby-artsplay/

No pre-registration necessary. Space is limited and admission to the class is limited to 15 children and their caregivers.

Join Reign Dance Project for Stories in Motion!

column1: Stories in Motion is a program that mixes literary and dance-based movement to help children learn to connect with stories by moving their bodies! During this 30-minute class, kids will work on skills that develop language, gross and fine motor movements, and practice following one and two step directions.

This class is designed to be unique to CMoR and was created with all kids in mind! We can’t wait to move with you!

Baby Artsplay!™ is back at CMoR!

column1: Classes at CMoR will be “drop-in style!” What does that mean? Simply join us on the 2nd Tuesday of the month @ 3:30PM.

Baby Artsplay!™ is a FREE program through Greater Richmond Wolf Trap offering children ages 3-36 months, along with their parents and caregivers, the opportunity to learn strategies for incorporating singing, dancing, drama, and other multi-sensory activities into their daily routine to increase engagement and support learning.
Baby Artsplay!™ is a program of Richmond Performing Arts Alliance. To learn more, click here: https://rpaalliance.com/baby-artsplay/

No pre-registration necessary. Space is limited and admission to the class is limited to 15 children and their caregivers.

Refined elegance and raw power take the stage in Moving Art Four: Director’s Choice.

The Leaves are Fading is a reflection on memory, love, and the passage of time set to the lush music of Antonín Dvořák. The elegant choreography of Antony Tudor — a pioneering British choreographer who revolutionized 20th century ballet — weaves together fleeting moments of romance in this poignant masterwork.

Spanish visionary and global icon Nacho Duato blends athletic contemporary movement with earthy sensuality to create a mesmerizing work that celebrates the universal power of music and dance.
